episode_title: How to Get Profitable AI: What the 6% Do Differently With Keith Jacobs and Grant Baldwin

real_qa.q: What percentage of AI investments show measurable ROI impact on company P&L according to recent studies?
real_qa.r: According to a McKinsey study of 1,700 companies, only 6 percent are making real money on AI. Of that 6 percent, 72 percent were successful because they redesigned how the work gets done. Most AI investments today show up nowhere on the P&L, meaning companies cannot prove that a dollar invested created measurable returns.
real_qa.requete: AI ROI success rate McKinsey study percentage

real_qa.q: Why does Genient employ anthropologists and psychologists before building AI software solutions?
real_qa.r: Genient staffs anthropologists and psychologists to conduct qualitative research and understand broken processes before designers begin work using AI. They observe what isn't working rather than asking clients what to build. Understanding the underlying motivations of humans and how job descriptions, org charts, and processes need to change is essential to building the right software and ensuring project success, not just building things right.
real_qa.requete: Genient anthropologists psychologists AI research why

real_qa.q: What is the 'Olympian worker' concept and how does it relate to AI automation in the workplace?
real_qa.r: The Olympian worker concept describes how AI automation removes busy work and administrative tasks, requiring employees to perform at a much higher cognitive level consistently. Just as only a few people can run a 100-meter dash in 10 seconds, not all workers will be able to adjust to having less busy work and more high cognitive work. Those who love their work will thrive, but those who just want routine tasks may struggle with this shift toward higher performance and continuous excellence.
real_qa.requete: Olympian worker AI automation workplace performance

real_qa.q: What is 'paving the cow path' and why is it a common mistake in AI implementation?
real_qa.r: Paving the cow path refers to automating existing broken processes rather than redesigning work from first principles. When an insurance benefits broker wanted AI to create the same manual spreadsheets their staff had always used, Genient instead showed them those spreadsheets were no longer needed. AI could automatically analyze data and triage next best actions, eliminating the need for four hours of manual work. The mistake is asking clients what they want rather than observing what they actually do and reimagining the process entirely.
real_qa.requete: paving the cow path AI implementation mistake

real_qa.q: What does Genient mean by 'behavior-first operating model' in AI transformation?
real_qa.r: Behavior-first operating model means conducting qualitative research to understand actual processes through observation, rather than creating McKinsey-style swim lane diagrams or asking departments what they want. By observing broken processes, teams inspire new models that differ from what quantitative analysis alone would produce. This approach generates evangelism and optimism as people see themselves in the new operating model, with improved roles, careers, jobs, and compensation.
real_qa.requete: behavior-first operating model Genient qualitative research

guest.bio_context: Keith Jacobs is co-CEO and partner at Genient, an AI and experience consultancy with a partnership history dating back before the dot-com boom. He previously worked as a developer during the dot-com era and has spent the past 20 years involved in companies and partnerships focused on redesigning how work gets done. At Genient, he leads qualitative research efforts using anthropologists and psychologists to understand broken processes before building AI-enabled solutions for Fortune 50 and mid-cap companies.
